Hi Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the checklist. I wanted to map out practical differences so procurement can choose with eyes open. TL;DR: all three paths work; tradeoffs below.

PO (net-30):
- What we need from you: signed PO with line items (SKU/name), billing address, remit-to (we'll supply), and PO number.
- Timeline: once PO is approved internally, we can start provisioning within 2 business days after receipt.
- Notes: standard for larger pilots; invoicing monthly.

Card payment:
- What we need: cardholder to sign SOW/accept terms; charge happens up front or on agreed billing cycle.
- Timeline: fastest provisioning (same day once we confirm card).
- Notes: preferred for very short pilots or evaluation.

Marketplace (AWS):
- What we need: confirmation you want to buy via AWS Marketplace and the target AWS account ID.
- Timeline: depends on marketplace listing and your internal approvers — sometimes faster, sometimes slower because it hits a different procurement flow.
- Notes: billing goes through marketplace (AWS invoices), which can change cost allocation and sometimes adds procurement fees. Also, we may have to surface a different vendor ID for your AP.

Attachments we can provide now:
- Redwood_W-9.pdf (attached previously)
- Sample invoice template (attached: Redwood_invoice_sample.pdf)
- Vendor portal invite (if you prefer portal onboarding: redwood-vendor-portal-invite.eml)

If Sara (AP) is the right contact, Jonas — can you loop her and I'll send the invoice template and remit instructions directly to speed the onboarding?

Happy to join a short call with Sara to clear any fields they require on the PO.

Thanks,
